judgment.notes: H002 supplies the differentiability required for both differentiations of H004. At t>0 a neighborhood lies in the domain. H005 applies at the fixed point and supplies exactly the scalar equation used in S002–S003. The routine facts in BG001–BG002 apply componentwise in finite-dimensional Euclidean space. No E/M applications occur.

Differentiating u·u=1 once gives F001; dotting H005 with u_t gives F002. Twice differentiating in time and each spatial coordinate yields exactly the two second-derivative identities. Dotting any normality equation with the unit vector u determines its scalar as the spatial gradient square minus the time derivative square; substitution using the existing witness gives the explicit equation. The signs and finite Laplacian sum agree with D002. Every output clause is proved. Only local derivatives are taken; there is no limit interchange or derivative of the scalar.

All three direct hypotheses are used. D002's smoothness guard is the direct input H002. F001 precedes F002, and both precede S003. The pointwise witness a comes from H005 under L1 and remains local. S003's scalar computation depends only on the equation for a, so its explicitly stated extension to every scalar satisfying that equation is legitimate universal conditional reasoning. The explicit PDE contains no private witness. L1 is discharged into t>0 and x,t are universally quantified; the coordinate j is locally arbitrary over 1 through n. No ancestor, circular premise or extra H is used.
